Information about a grading setup can reach a model through many channels: the prompt itself, file and directory names, hidden instructions, test outputs, logs, environment variables, documentation, and even the structure of examples. Each of these can act as a backchannel that tells the model something about what the grader expects, the score it is being optimized for, or the exact format that will be rewarded. Careful design and systematic auditing of the evaluation environment are needed to keep those channels closed.
